findings.title: Midnight timestamps are expanded into whole-day bounds
findings.description: Pydantic parses `"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"` as a `date` in this date-first union, verified with `TypeAdapter`. Consequently, `resolve_window` expands an explicit midnight `end` to 23:59:59.999999, returning almost an extra day of data. Both endpoints are affected. Distinguish bare dates from timestamps before union coercion, and add regression tests for explicit midnight bounds.

findings.title: Response construction blocks the event loop
findings.description: Only database work runs in the executor; model construction and serialization run synchronously on the event loop. An isolated benchmark of the actual candle-model code at 75,000 rows took approximately 591 ms to build and 470 ms to dump, excluding encoding. This substantially exceeds the required sub-millisecond synchronous budget and stalls unrelated requests. Offload construction and serialization after releasing the connection, including the equivalent trades path. Add a load test measuring unrelated-request responsiveness during large responses.

findings.title: Concurrent ingestion can bypass the row ceiling
findings.description: Count and fetch are separate statements without a stable snapshot. The pool configuration does not establish repeatable-read isolation, so ingestion committed between them can increase the fetched result beyond `max_rows`. Admission subsequently checks the old count, not the fetched length. The candle path has the same race; batch ingestion means the excess need not be just one row. Use a consistent snapshot or reject oversized fetched results, and test an insert committed between count and fetch.
